title: The verb: aspect, tense, person, mood, voice

blocks.text: A grammatical category that expresses how a verbal action, event, or state, extends over time.
A grammatical aspect that describes an action viewed as a simple whole.
A grammatical aspect used for ongoing, habitual, repeated, or similar semantic roles, whether they are in the past, present, or future.
The property of indicating the point in time at which an action or state of being occurs or exists.
A grammatical tense whose principal function is to locate a situation or event in the present time.
A grammatical tense whose function is to place an action or situation in the past.
The tense or time form of a verb used to refer to an event or occurrence that has not yet happened or is expected to happen in the future.
A linguistic category used to distinguish between the speaker of an utterance and those to whom or about whom they are speaking.
A verb form that depends on how its containing clause relates to the speaker’s or writer’s wish, intent, or assertion about reality.
The mood of a verb used in ordinary, factual, or objective statements.
The grammatical mood generally expressing a command, though also used to express a request or permission.
сослагательное наклонение — subjunctive or conditional mood
Mood expressing an action or state which is hypothetical or anticipated rather than actual, including wishes and commands.
A particular way of inflecting or conjugating verbs, or a particular form of a verb, which indicates the relation of the subject of the verb to the action which the verb expresses.
The form in which the subject of a verb carries out some action.
The form of a transitive verb in which its subject receives the action.
The act or process of conjugating a verb.

A non-finite verb form considered neutral with respect to inflection; depending on language variously found used with auxiliary verbs, in subordinate clauses, or acting as a gerund, and often as the dictionary form.
A verb whose subject and direct object are the same.
A verb that is accompanied (either clearly or implicitly) by a direct object in the active voice.
Exercises: the terms themselves, written from their English; then which term a definition describes; then the terms matched to their English. Review Terms, above, drills this lesson's terms.
